stories.headline: US index futures recover after sharp early post-election losses
stories.body: Reuters reported earlier falls of as much as 2.4% for Nasdaq-100 futures and 1.4% for S&P 500 futures. At 3:13 a.m. ET on 4 November, Dow futures were up 0.46%, S&P 500 futures up 0.15% and Nasdaq-100 futures up 0.26%. These were intraday observations, not live quotes; the earlier trough times were not established.
stories.analysis: Reversal highlights repricing uncertainty and does not prove steady rate or FX response.
stories.watch_next: US open, US Treasury curve and Big Tech regulation
stories.earlier: The previous v4 documented projected Democratic control of both US congressional chambers without a verified, time-matched market reaction.

stories.headline: UOB lowers full-year margin forecast after Q3 profit misses estimates
stories.body: UOB reported Q3 net profit of S$1.25 billion against the S$1.35 billion LSEG mean estimate from two analysts. Q3 net interest margin was 1.68%, down six basis points quarter-on-quarter. Management expects full-year NIM below 1.75%, versus previous guidance of 1.75%–1.80%. Reuters observed shares down over 5% to S$38.15; observation time not established. This is a catch-up story from an earlier reporting window.
stories.analysis: Deposit competition pressures banks margins; avoid generalising sector.
stories.watch_next: Upcoming DBS and OCBC earnings

stories.headline: French services contract as Germany and Italy maintain growth
stories.body: October services PMI readings: France 46.2, down from 51.2 in September and below a 48.4 flash estimate; Germany 52.5, from 52.9; Italy 52.0, from 51.7 and above a Reuters survey forecast of 51.5. Italy's selling-price PMI rose to 55.9 from 54.8 and input prices to 68.4 from 65.4. PMI values are diffusion indices, not annual inflation percentages.
stories.analysis: French contraction with Italian cost pressure complicates ECB assessment.
stories.watch_next: Euro area aggregate PMI, inflation and ECB guidance

stories.headline: Google confirms June expansion of voluntary exit offers across five countries
stories.body: Google confirmed voluntary exit packages offered in June 2026 to certain employees in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland. The number who accepted has not been established. Reuters sources said the Swiss programme excluded DeepMind. November reporting newly disclosed an existing initiative, not fresh layoffs.
stories.analysis: Cost controls accompanying AI capex; no quantified savings demonstrated.
stories.watch_next: Alphabet employee changes, severance and AI capex economics

stories.headline: Emaar proposes voluntary minority buyout of Emaar Development
stories.body: Emaar Properties, which owns just over 79% of Emaar Development, plans a voluntary cash offer of AED 15 per share for the remainder, potentially worth up to US$3.43 billion. Reuters observed Emaar Development up 5.3% at AED 14.64 by 06:30 UTC before article publication. The offer is not completed and funding details are unverified. This article is a catch-up discovery.
stories.analysis: Potential funding and leverage impact, pending terms.
stories.watch_next: Offer acceptance, acquisition financing and delisting decision

stories.headline: Goodman and Digital Realty offer up to A$715m for a minority stake in NextDC
stories.body: According to a term sheet, the pair offered to buy up to 9.9% of NextDC for approximately A$715 million (US$499.7 million). Their offer of A$9.50 a share was 45.5% above NextDC's A$6.53 Wednesday closing price. NextDC had previously said electricity grid upgrades would defer about A$140 million of contracted revenue in the current financial year and has shelved new development projects. Market evidence: Reuters gave the historical A$6.53 Wednesday closing price; no post-offer trading price or change reported.
stories.analysis: A prospective strategic shareholder investment could address confidence and financing pressure, but neither a completed deal nor a new cash injection is established. AI data centres still face power-grid execution risk.
stories.watch_next: Offer completion, whether capital actually reaches NextDC, debt and grid milestones.

stories.headline: Binance customers have withdrawn a net US$4.72bn after exchange reopening
stories.body: Reuters' newly published crypto roundup reported net customer withdrawals of US$4.72 billion after Binance reopened following last week's hack. Bitcoin was quoted at US$78,070 by 07:15 GMT on 4 November after briefly touching a six-week low. That historical price is not a live quote. Reuters said the wider crypto market lost about US$300 billion in value over the previous month, and investors were also weighing US election implications. Market evidence: Reuters Bitcoin observation: approximately US$78,070 at 07:15 GMT (15:15 SGT); not price movement solely attributable to the earlier hack or today's election.
stories.analysis: Large exchange withdrawals highlight custody and platform liquidity risk, but are not proof of insolvency or a bank credit default; the hack and withdrawals predate this primary hour.
stories.watch_next: Whether net withdrawals continue, user access and verifiable reserves; new investigations or regulator decisions.

stories.headline: Smith+Nephew cuts annual forecasts and confirms J&J orthopaedics merger talks ended
stories.body: Smith+Nephew said merger talks with Johnson & Johnson's orthopaedics business held earlier this year have ended. Smith+Nephew lowered its full-year revenue and profit guidance due to persistent weakness in its Orthopaedics division. The company said it would continue evaluating strategic options for the division. Market evidence: No attributable share-price move in the inspected Reuters article.
stories.analysis: Reduced guidance worsens the earnings/cash-generation outlook, while failed merger talks remove a potential strategic outcome; final debt implications are not established.
stories.watch_next: Updated numerical guidance, restructuring plans, strategic alternatives and refinancing needs.

stories.headline: IndiGo in early talks for 100 Embraer regional jets, sources say
stories.body: Three people told Reuters IndiGo was discussing a possible purchase of 100 Embraer regional jets, with options for about 50 more. Neither the model nor quantity was settled and no contract was announced; deliveries would likely begin in or after 2030. Reuters said that the 100 aircraft alone could be worth billions of dollars at list prices, before commonly negotiated discounts. Market evidence: No attributable share-price movement reported.
stories.analysis: If signed, the order would create major future aircraft financing and fleet-capital-expenditure needs; no financing terms or confirmed obligation exist today.
stories.watch_next: Binding purchase agreement, aircraft model, delivery slots, financing/leasing terms.

stories.headline: Security sources report two drone attacks on Iranian Kurdish opposition in Iraq
stories.body: Reuters cited security sources saying two explosive-laden drones attacked Iranian Kurdish opposition groups in Iraq's Sulaymaniyah and east Erbil on Wednesday. The article noted Iran has struck these groups' bases before; the specific attacker, damage and casualties from this incident were not verified. Market evidence: No attributable crude oil, gold or currency move reported in the inspected source.
stories.analysis: This may add to regional escalation risk, but a direct oil-supply disruption is not established by the report.
stories.watch_next: Independent identification of the attackers, damage assessments and any response affecting energy routes.

stories.headline: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy-pill sales beat estimates; 2026 guidance raised
stories.body: Wegovy pill third-quarter revenue DKK5.39bn, versus company-compiled consensus DKK4.62bn, up 53% from Q2. Adjusted operating profit DKK31.72bn vs DKK28.39bn expected; adjusted sales DKK79.20bn vs DKK73.22bn expected. Adjusted 2026 sales and operating-profit outlook at constant exchange rates raised to -2% through +2% from previous -6% through 0%.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: Positive oral-obesity-drug adoption and better operating profits; monitor competitive pricing, Lilly market share and sustainability of guidance.
stories.watch_next: Wegovy pill market share, 2026 profit delivery and forthcoming Lilly results.

stories.headline: Continental raises 2026 operating-margin outlook on tyre strength
stories.body: Continental raised FY2026 operating profit margin guidance excluding discontinued ContiTech to 13.4%-14%. Previous range was 12%-13.5%; company-supplied analyst consensus stood at 13.7%.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: Better tyre margins modestly improve earnings expectations; does not imply a broad recovery in European manufacturing.
stories.watch_next: Actual reported margins, tyre demand, restructuring and credit metrics.

stories.headline: Reuters relays unconfirmed FT report of Oracle–Tencent US$7bn AI deal cancellation
stories.body: Reuters relayed a Financial Times report alleging cancellation of an estimated US$7 billion Oracle–Tencent AI-chip lease involving about 100,000 chips at Southeast Asian data centres. Reuters could not independently verify the claim; company confirmation was unavailable.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: If confirmed, trade controls could alter cloud revenue assumptions, asset utilisation and China/SEA data-centre buildout financing. Cancellation is not confirmed by Oracle or Reuters independently.
stories.watch_next: Official Oracle/Tencent statements, contractual status, cancellation costs and further US export-policy clarifications.

stories.headline: Meta US$15bn bond offering: 2031 and 2033 tranche coupons reviewed
stories.body: The Reuters account gives US$3.25 billion of Meta notes due in 2031 carrying a 5.85% coupon and US$3.25 billion due in 2033 at a 6.25% coupon, with Moody's assigning Aa3. The time these terms first appeared is unknown. Coupon does not establish issue yield.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: Coupon and issue yield are not interchangeable; credit evaluation requires final issue price, maturity-specific UST spreads, leverage and expected capex.
stories.watch_next: Full tranche pricing, issue yields, benchmark spreads and free-cash-flow/debt trajectory.

The election overview's exact revision time was not confirmed, and no event-timed market move was verified.

A presidential spokesperson said the allegations could amount to treason and threaten national security. These remain allegations, not convictions; an exact dismissal time and attributable financial-market reaction were not verified.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: The dismissal creates governance uncertainty in a major Southeast Asian economy, but no economic-policy impact or quantified market repricing has been established.
stories.watch_next: Investigation findings, appointment of a replacement and any confirmed policy or rupiah, bond or equity-market developments.

stories.headline: Iran Revolutionary Guard claims four oil tankers hit naval mines and two vessels seized near Hormuz
stories.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed four tankers struck naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz and remained ablaze or destroyed; it also claimed two other vessels were seized. Reuters attributed these statements to the IRGC and did not independently verify tanker losses, identify ships, or establish an event time. No time-matched market-price reaction was established.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: If independently confirmed, mine hazards and tanker damage could disrupt oil supply, shipping and marine insurance; the claims are not confirmation of actual losses.
stories.watch_next: Verify vessels and maritime-authority reports, plus Reuters-observed tanker traffic and oil or freight market reactions.

stories.headline: Further Republican-held US Senate seats flip in media projections: Texas, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa
stories.body: Reuters reported US media projections of Democratic Senate wins by James Talarico over Ken Paxton in Texas, Sherrod Brown over Jon Husted in Ohio's special election, Adam Hamilton over Roger Marshall in Kansas and Josh Turek over Ashley Hinson in Iowa. Republicans entered the election with a 53–47 Senate majority; Democrats needed a net gain of four seats. Results are media projections, not certification. No market reaction attributable to these specific calls was verified.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: Additional pickups change the Senate-control outlook and potentially fiscal-policy negotiations, but do not themselves quantify a Treasury or foreign-exchange market reaction.
stories.watch_next: Remaining Senate races, confirmed majority balance, certification, and measured US rates, FX and equity reactions.
stories.earlier: Previous v2 (11:47:09 AM SGT) covered the projected Democratic House majority and individual seat flips, with Senate control unsettled. Reuters now reports four further projected Democratic Senate pickups in Texas, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa.

stories.headline: UAE non-oil firms increase selling prices at fastest pace since PMI survey began in 2009
stories.body: S&P Global reported UAE non-oil PMI of 54.8 in October versus 55.3 in September, above the 50 expansion threshold. Reuters said selling prices rose at the fastest rate since the survey began in August 2009, while input-cost inflation was highest since June 2022, including raw materials, fuel, energy and freight. New orders accelerated; employment edged down. No attributable market reaction was verified.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: Strong demand coexists with price pressure that may affect borrowers' margins and regional credit; this PMI is not an observed CPI surprise.
stories.watch_next: Subsequent UAE inflation and PMI releases and corporate margin developments.

stories.analysis: A regional security risk relevant to Asian risk sentiment, but no evidence from the cited report of an immediate FX/portfolio repricing.
stories.watch_next: Missile classification, allied response and regional-market implications if Reuters subsequently establishes them.

stories.headline: Industry data show US crude inventories unexpectedly fall 5.27 million barrels
stories.body: Market sources citing API indicated US crude stocks decreased 5.27 million barrels in the week ended 30 October; eight Reuters-polled analysts expected an increase of about 880,000 barrels. Reuters observed Brent down 26 cents to US$103.34 and WTI down 53 cents to US$95.56 at 01:57 UTC, before this Reuters article publication. Official EIA crude inventory release scheduled for 4 Nov 15:30 UTC / 23:30 SGT, not yet available as of cutoff.
stories.analysis: Larger-than-expected industry stock draw is supportive for physical oil balance, while geopolitical and demand expectations could dominate price; compare with official EIA data before extrapolating.
stories.watch_next: Official EIA inventory report 4 Nov 23:30 SGT; Middle East developments and Brent/WTI movements.

stories.watch_next: Restructuring execution, renewal trends, remaining workforce capacity and margins.

stories.headline: Suncor beats quarterly profit estimates and raises dividend

stories.analysis: Elevated oil and refining margins can improve integrated energy cash flows while increasing cost pressure elsewhere; a single quarter is not a forward oil-price forecast.
stories.watch_next: Dividend funding, realised refinery margins and next-quarter crude pricing.

sources.title: AMD forecasts quarterly revenue above estimates as data-center growth accelerates
Super Micro forecasts quarterly revenue above estimates on strong AI server demand
Block raises full-year profit outlook as Cash App drives Q3 growth
LATAM Airlines trims earnings outlook as fuel costs bite
Amgen third quarter sales rise 8%, led by cholesterol, cancer drugs

stories.headline: AMD beats quarterly estimates and forecasts further data-centre growth
stories.body: Fourth-quarter revenue guidance approximately $17 billion plus or minus 3%, versus LSEG consensus $16.23 billion. Third-quarter revenue $13.38 billion, +45%; data-center revenue $8.55 billion, +97%. Adjusted EPS $2.09 versus $1.95 consensus; guided adjusted gross margin approximately 55% versus 55.27% consensus. Reuters reported AMD shares rising more than 6% in extended trading; exact observation time not verified.
stories.analysis: AI demand is supporting revenue, but gross-margin guidance slightly below consensus raises a profitability watchpoint.
stories.watch_next: Helios rack ramp, Meta deployments, margin and memory supply; full earnings follow-up.

stories.headline: Super Micro raises FY2027 sales forecast on AI-server demand
stories.body: First-quarter revenue $19.95 billion versus LSEG consensus $16.39 billion; adjusted EPS $1.81 versus $1.23 consensus. Next-quarter revenue outlook $19.5-$21.5 billion versus $17.14 billion consensus. FY2027 forecast raised to $72.0-$82.0 billion from $65.0-$72.0 billion.
stories.analysis: AI server demand supports growth, but scaling and export-control compliance remain material execution risks.
stories.watch_next: Gross margins, working capital, cash conversion and export-control compliance.

stories.headline: Block raises gross profit guidance as receivables losses rise
stories.body: 2026 gross profit outlook raised to $12.63 billion from $12.51 billion. Cash App gross profit +27% year-on-year in Q3; Square gross profit +14%. Losses on transaction, loan and consumer receivables rose 65.6% to $601.7 million in Q3; the specific comparison period for this figure was not stated in the inspected report.
stories.analysis: Consumer payment growth is strong, but credit losses matter for risk-adjusted profitability; not evidence of sector-wide delinquencies.
stories.watch_next: Receivables losses, repayment trends, 2027 gross profit guidance and source of AI-related revenue.

stories.headline: LATAM cuts 2026 EBITDA outlook on fuel cost pressure
stories.body: Adjusted 2026 EBITDA guidance cut to $3.9-$4.05 billion from $4.1-$4.4 billion. Q3 revenue $4.57 billion and adjusted EBITDA $1.10 billion versus LSEG consensus $1.05 billion. Average fuel prices increased more than 50% versus year earlier, costing approximately $520 million in Q3.
stories.analysis: An airline can experience resilient demand yet face margin pressure if fuel costs rise faster than fares.
stories.watch_next: Fuel prices, capacity adjustment, operating margin and debt-servicing flexibility.

stories.headline: Amgen raises 2026 outlook after earnings beat
stories.body: Third-quarter revenue $10.4 billion versus $10.1 billion consensus; adjusted EPS $6.45 versus $5.79 consensus. 2026 adjusted EPS range raised to $22.90-$23.70 from $22.30-$23.50. 2026 revenue outlook raised to $38.9-$39.7 billion from $38.2-$39.4 billion.
stories.analysis: Stronger drug portfolio sales support guidance; clinical and competitive risks remain.
stories.watch_next: Drug pipeline trial data, Repatha competitive pressure, execution of revised guidance.

sources.title: SK Hynix's New York chip plans hit snag over US restrictions on China, sources say
BMW lowers 2026 automotive EBIT margin outlook and deliveries
Bundesbank's Nagel joins ECB chorus backing December rate hike
China to raise FX reserve requirement to slow yuan's rally
Virgin Media O2 to cut thousands of jobs and halt UK fibre expansion

stories.headline: SK Hynix US chip expansion faces China export-licence obstacle
stories.body: US officials have not approved the equipment-export licences sought for SK Hynix Dalian expansion, according to Reuters sources. Solidigm is considering about US$45 billion investment in New York NAND facilities, potentially about US$100 billion over time; no location decision made. Officials have not formally rejected the requested licences.
stories.analysis: US-China technology restrictions may delay or complicate financing a large US semiconductor buildout; a proposal is not committed capital expenditure.
stories.watch_next: US Commerce and White House export-licence decisions; formal Solidigm investment announcement.

stories.headline: BMW cuts 2026 automotive margin and delivery outlook
stories.body: BMW lowered its 2026 automotive EBIT margin forecast to negative 0.5% to positive 0.5%. BMW expects a moderate decrease in automotive deliveries in 2026. BMW will accelerate management-function reductions.
stories.analysis: Reduced margins merit closer attention to automotive cash flow and credit quality; resulting cash-flow amount was not quantified in this Reuters article.
stories.watch_next: Full earnings detail, operating cash flow, restructuring costs and deliveries.

stories.headline: Bundesbank Nagel backs likely December ECB rate hike
stories.body: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said a December ECB rate hike appears very likely necessary absent a significantly improved inflation outlook. ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5% last week. Investors were pricing two to three rate hikes over the coming year, according to Reuters; a December increase was not fully priced in.
stories.analysis: Hawkish ECB commentary reinforces euro-area funding-rate sensitivity, without confirming a policy decision or quantifying a new yield move.
stories.watch_next: December ECB decision, inflation data and subsequent repricing.

stories.headline: PBOC raises FX deposit reserve ratio to 6% from 4%
stories.body: PBOC announced the FX deposit reserve requirement ratio will rise by two percentage points to 6% from 4% effective 15 November 2026. Reuters calculates that the measure absorbs US$24 billion in FX liquidity. Onshore yuan weakened as much as 0.37% to 6.6728 per dollar after the announcement; exact price observation time not independently verified.
stories.analysis: The policy signals PBOC concern about one-way yuan appreciation and alters bank FX liquidity; it does not establish USD/SGD or USD/CHF moves.
stories.watch_next: 15 November implementation, USD/CNH responses and daily PBOC fixings.

stories.headline: Virgin Media O2 targets restructuring as high debt weighs
stories.body: Virgin Media O2 reports £22 billion of debt, equal to 5.6 times annualised third-quarter core earnings. Management targets £800 million savings by 2029, partly through reducing wage costs by 30%. Plans for fibre expansion have been curtailed amid competition and regulatory obstacles.
stories.analysis: Illustrates leverage, constrained organic investment and competitive pressure in the telecom sector, but Reuters did not report a default.
stories.watch_next: Refinancing terms, net leverage, cash generation and execution of savings.

stories.headline: Polymarket unit approved by NFA to be futures broker
stories.body: The US National Futures Association approved Polymarket unit PM Derivatives LLC as a futures commission merchant. US CFTC authorisation remains required before it can act as a broker. The firm intends to run fully collateralised positions.
stories.analysis: Regulatory progress, but licensing and protection of customer funds remain unresolved.
stories.watch_next: Watch CFTC authorisation, actual operational start and customer-fund safeguards.

stories.headline: Congo opens mining fraud probe following copper and cobalt seizures
stories.body: DR Congo ordered investigations into suspected mining fraud and smuggling following seizure of more than 500 trucks and thousands of metric tons of copper and cobalt. Authorities separately reported over 500 pieces of equipment seized at an ERG-owned site and more than 60 foreign nationals detained. Allegations remain under investigation.
stories.analysis: Critical minerals supply-chain compliance risk; no global shortage confirmed.
stories.watch_next: Watch formal findings, production disruptions and metals-supply effects.

stories.headline: Shell agrees to sell North West Shelf LNG stake to XRG
stories.body: Shell agreed to sell its 16.67% non-operated North West Shelf LNG interest to ADNOC subsidiary XRG for US$1.45 billion base consideration, with possible milestone-linked payments. The buyer assumes decommissioning obligations; closing is expected in 2027.
stories.analysis: LNG asset rotation; project liabilities and contingent terms matter.
stories.watch_next: Watch transaction approvals, contingent payments, decommissioning liabilities and actual LNG flows.

stories.topic: US fiscal policy / Middle East / energy and rates
stories.headline: Trump says US will end annual funding to Israel after 2026; implementation unclear
stories.body: Reuters reported on 3 November that President Trump said he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu agreed to end $4 billion in annual US funding after 2026, while weapons sales could continue. Reuters noted that an existing $3.8 billion annual military-aid arrangement runs through September 2028 and that appropriations require congressional action. Separately, Reuters described an earlier market session with Brent down 2.9% at $101.75 per barrel and the US 10-year Treasury yield up 2.5 basis points to 4.9187%. These are historical market observations, not quotes at this hourly cutoff; exact intraday observation times were not independently verified.
stories.analysis: Interpretation: Uncertainty around implementation could affect geopolitical risk perceptions, oil prices and inflation-sensitive bond yields. The announcement does not establish that the aid has already stopped or supply a fresh FX conversion trigger.
stories.watch_next: Watch White House and Israeli clarification, US congressional appropriations and verified market reaction.
